thread_analysis.thread_summary: [COMPANY] finalizes three separate Bluetooth registrations. The thread clarifies that a yellow warning mark on Design Details in the Submission Requirements simply reflects that the registration doesn't include a Host layer (not a blocking issue), and that since this particular order did not include compliance folder creation as a service, the customer (as Listing Owner) is responsible for creating their own compliance folder per Bluetooth SIG's QPRDv3 specification and retaining it for the standard post-end-of-sales period.
all_questions_found: Does the Review Page content look correct, and should Submission proceed despite the yellow warning mark shown on Design Details?
What does the yellow warning mark on Design Details in the Submission Requirements actually indicate?
Since this order did not include compliance folder creation, who is responsible for creating it, and what should the customer reference to do so themselves?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread clarifies that a yellow warning mark on Design Details within Submission Requirements can simply reflect that the registration does not include a Host layer (such as a Controller-only or Component-only registration), which is an informational notice rather than a blocking issue, and Submission can proceed normally. It also clarifies that when an engagement's scope does not include compliance folder creation as a service, the customer (as Listing Owner) must create their own compliance folder, following Bluetooth SIG's own QPRDv3 specification section 3.4.1 ('Compliance Folder'), and retain it for the standard post-end-of-sales period for SIG audit purposes -- the consultant instead provides the registration-completion SDoC (Supplier's Declaration of Conformity) documents and registration detail page links as proof of completion.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: A yellow warning mark on Design Details that reflects only the absence of a Host layer in the registration is not a blocking issue and should not be treated as requiring correction before Submission. When an engagement's scope does not include compliance folder creation, the customer themselves is responsible for assembling it according to Bluetooth SIG's own QPRDv3 'Compliance Folder' specification, rather than assuming the consultant will provide one as part of the deliverables.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Treating the Design Details warning mark as a problem requiring correction, rather than recognizing it as an expected notice for a registration without a Host layer, could cause unnecessary delay. Assuming a compliance folder will be automatically provided when the engagement's scope does not include it would leave the customer without the documentation required to respond to a future SIG audit.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a yellow warning mark appears on Design Details for a registration that doesn't include a Host layer, recognize it as an expected informational notice rather than a blocking issue. When quoting or completing an engagement, be explicit about whether compliance folder creation is included in scope -- if not, point the customer to QPRDv3 section 3.4.1 so they can assemble and retain their own compliance folder for SIG audit purposes.
